countries.name: Slovakia

countries.name: Poland
countries.note: Crypto-to-crypto swaps are taxable – calculate each disposal’s PLN gain/loss.

countries.name: Austria
countries.note: Staking and lending rewards are taxed when received, not when sold.

countries.name: Germany
countries.note: Crypto-to-crypto is taxable within the first year. FIFO record-keeping is critical.

countries.name: Hungary
countries.note: Documented acquisition costs are deductible – keep every invoice.

countries.name: Slovenia
countries.gainTax: Progressive, up to ~50 % on disposal gains
countries.note: Cryptocurrency gains are treated as income; verify current guidance with a local advisor.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.note: Digital-asset regime is new (2024+) – rules are still being interpreted in practice.

countries.name: Romania
countries.note: 10 % is among the lowest flat rates in the EU – deduct your cost basis.

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.note: Low flat rate; keep exchange statements for audit-ready records.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.gainTax: Box 3 wealth tax on deemed return (~36 % on fictional yield)
countries.note: No capital-gains tax per se – you are taxed on assumed return of your holdings. Box 3 is under reform – verify the current year’s rules.
